hints.title: Rooted Multiplicative Tree
hints.text: The unit conversion relations form a directed graph where unit 0 serves as the reference base with conversion multiplier 1.

hints.title: Traverse Hierarchy from Root
hints.text: Traverse connections starting from unit 0 and propagate conversion multipliers along each edge.

hints.title: Modulo Multiplication
hints.text: Multiply parent factor by edge weight modulo 10^9 + 7.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def baseUnitConversions(self, conversions: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        MOD = 1_000_000_007
        n = len(conversions) + 1
        ans = [0] * n
        ans[0] = 1
        graph = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v, factor in conversions:
            graph[u].append((v, factor))
        q = deque([0])
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            for v, factor in graph[u]:
                ans[v] = (ans[u] * factor) % MOD
                q.append(v)
        return ans
```

variables: N: total number of distinct units
complexity.notes: Breadth-first traversal visits each node and conversion edge once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Redundant depth searches from non-root sources do extra work.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Adjacency list stores the conversion tree in linear space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Traverse the tree from unit 0 applying modular multiplication.
